newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude firm, off highs in tentative market.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude firm, off highs in tentative market.

text.p: NYMEX crude remained firm into Monday afternoon on this morning's news that a power outage took out one million barrels per day in crude throughput from Interprovincial Pipe Line's (IPL) huge system.
But, oil prices were off from their highs as traders were scared to increase long positions after a string of late session sell-offs last week.
At 1422 EDT, May crude was up 33 cents at $19.45 a barrel, off its session high of $19.62 made early session.

"Almost every single day last week we sold off near the close, so traders are not sure that today will be any different," said Ed Kevelson, director of refined products at Paribas Futures Inc in New York.
May heating oil was up 0.21 cent at 53.35 cents a gallon after rising as high as 54.50 cents, and May gasoline was up 0.42 cent at 60.90 cents gallon after rising as high as 61.50 cents.
Spot gasoline faced increasing technical resistance, failing near Friday's high of 61.60 which in turn failed near Thursday's high of 61.70.
IPL said Monday that a severe snowstorm in the U.S. Northern Plains caused a power outage in Minnesota that hit three pumping stations on its pipeline system.
The IPL system had been carrying 1.4 million bpd and comprises several pipelines that run from western Canada through the U.S. Midwest to Quebec and upstate New York.
The lines that are shut carry light, medium, heavy and synthetic crudes plus condesate.

"That's a lot of volume (to be shut), and for crude and products to be off from their highs could indicate how sick the market may be," said Andy Lebow, trader with E. D. & F. Man International in New York.
Last week, prompt crude lost almost $1.75 a barrel on views of ample supply driven by increasing imports.
IPL said that it would not be until Wednesday at the earliest until the pumping stations could resume operations.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
